title: Is the quotient always greater when the divisor is a decimal?
description: Twelve point five is divided by two point five, by one and by zero point five, and the three results are put in a table. Keeko doubts that a decimal divisor always gives a bigger answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the divisor with one, not with a counting number. Watch for children who think every decimal divisor makes the answer bigger.

source: Is the quotient always greater than the dividend when the divisor is a decimal? Test 12.5 ÷ 2.5, 12.5 ÷ 1 and 12.5 ÷ 0.5, and make a table.
video_script.why: The child has seen that dividing by zero point four gives a bigger number, and now tests whether every decimal divisor does the same.
video_script.substitution: the book's own three divisions of twelve point five, and the table that sorts them
video_script.anchor: Twelve point five divided by two point five, by one and by zero point five
video_script.wrong_answer: a decimal divisor always gives a bigger answer
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip thinks any decimal divisor gives a bigger answer. But two point five is a decimal that is more than one, and twelve point five divided by it is only five.
video_script.payoff_line: A decimal divisor does not always give a bigger quotient.

final_answer.value: No. Divisor greater than 1: quotient smaller; divisor 1: equal; divisor between 0 and 1: quotient greater
final_answer.spoken: no. A divisor more than one gives a smaller quotient, a divisor of one gives an equal quotient, and a divisor between zero and one gives a greater quotient

maths_rules: table: divisor more than 1, quotient smaller; divisor 1, quotient equal; divisor between 0 and 1, quotient greater
video_script.design: One idea: the size of the quotient depends on whether the divisor is more than one, equal to one, or less than one. Assumes multiplying both numbers by ten. Wrong idea: any decimal divisor gives a bigger answer. The three divisions stay all video; the table builds in the last step; the rule appears on the answer beat.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>The divisor, two point five, is more than one, and five is smaller than twelve point five.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks a decimal divisor always gives a bigger answer.
